title: Seazn capture record, v1: POST /api/v1/capture/codes/{code}/records (PROPOSED)
description: PROPOSED, design only (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-capture-record-upload-design.md, for owner review): no route serves it yet and no zod twin mirrors it; the path is a proposal. The operator's Send record tap (owner rulings R3, R4) posts the phone's scrubbed session record as NDJSON (application/x-ndjson): one JSON object per line, and THIS schema is ONE line. Limits apply to the DECOMPRESSED body: at most 1000 non-empty lines and at most 1 MB (1048576 bytes). Content-Encoding: gzip is accepted; the server inflates at most 1 MB + 1 byte and stops there, so a zip bomb is 413 too_large and is never inflated whole. The keys are capture's modules/capture-engine/src/scrub/allow-list.json (capture 7ea8f63): at, kind and level are the line's own; every plain, publicUrl, text and scalars key under its class, a field named like a line key written field_<key>. Any other key, a never key included (even masked), is 422 invalid, and so is a value off its key's class. Beyond any shape, the server refuses with 422 invalid a body in which any string value is secret-shaped: S1 the Bearer token that sent the record, raw, percent-encoded or form-encoded; S2 an ingest URL (rtmp://, rtmps:// or srt://); S3 a streamid= or passphrase= pair; S4 a URL with userinfo (scheme://...@); S5 a Bearer credential (the word Bearer followed by a value). The 422's message names the line number and the key, never the value. Attribution: the record is the phone's last 1000 lines and can span codes. The server keeps a line only if it belongs to the sending code, and drops every other line before storing: A1 a line whose sid is a string is kept iff that session belongs to the sending code; A2 a line with no sid is kept iff it falls inside a pairing window of the sending code: a window opens at a `pair` line whose tokenTag is the tag of a token of the sending code, and runs through the next `unpaired` or `ended` line, or up to (not including) the next `pair` line, whichever comes first. A line before the record's first `pair` line is in no window. A dropped line is counted, never stored, logged or echoed. $defs.ok is the 201 answer and $defs.refusal every refusal body (the capture envelope {code, message}: the phone keys on code; message is a developer string the phone never shows). Its sha256 and fixtures are pinned by apps/web/src/server/api-v1/__tests__/capture-contract.test.ts.

at.description: When the line was written, ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z, as both of capture's writers spell it (IsoTime.utc and Date.toISOString: milliseconds, e.g. 2026-10-11T21:19:03.123Z). NOT epoch milliseconds: the design brief said ms epoch, and capture's writers say otherwise (spec 2026-10-12, Premise P1).

kind.description: What the line records: a plain word (capture's modules/capture-engine/src/scrub/allow-list.json, its `kinds`), or the mask *** when capture's scrub masked it. A kind outside capture's list is admitted: the list grows with the app, and a word is not a secret.

level.description: debug, warn or error; ABSENT means info, which capture never writes (CD7). info is admitted when sent, and the mask *** is native's answer to a level it does not vet.

ok.description: 201: the record was received. The bare shape, never an {ok, data} envelope. Owner ruling 2026-10-12: the app shows ONLY the ref ("Sent — ref R-7K2Q") and says nothing about dropped lines; the server still returns and records both counts, and kept + dropped is the number of non-empty lines received. A record whose every line was dropped is still 201 (kept 0), stored as counts with no lines.

ref.description: The record's reference, for the operator to read to the organiser: R- and four characters of upper-case Crockford base32 (no I, L, O or U), e.g. R-7K2Q; the server may lengthen it to eight without a new version. Unique among the records still kept.

kept.description: Lines stored: those that belong to the sending code (A1, A2).

dropped.description: Lines dropped as another code's. The app ignores it (owner ruling 2026-10-12).

refusal.description: Every refusal: 401 code_ended (a missing, malformed or wrong Bearer, an unknown code, an ended code: one sentence, no oracle), 404 not_a_stream_code (a malformed code), 413 too_large (over 1000 lines or 1 MB decompressed; a NEW word, proposed), 422 invalid (not NDJSON, an empty record, a key or value off the allow-list, a secret-shaped value, an unsupported Content-Encoding), 429 rate_limited (10 records an hour per code, with Retry-After), 503 unavailable (anything unmapped). Never replaced: a replaced phone may send (R4).

code.description: The machine word the phone keys on.

message.description: A plain English developer string; the phone never shows it. It never quotes a line's value.
